Start with a show of hands. Read the question, then go through the four options and ask people to put their hand up for the one they think is biggest. Most people pick driving or flying. Click once to reveal: it’s heat.

The answer

Heat.

37%

of the world’s energy CO₂ comes from making heat.

Heat: about half of all energy we use

Transport: about 30%

Electricity for everything else: about 20%

Sources: IEA Renewables 2025 (37% of energy-related CO₂, 2024 data); IEA Renewables 2021 (shares of final energy use).

It’s heat. Making heat causes 37% of the world’s energy CO₂, more than transport or electricity.

Closer to home

18%

of all UK emissions come from heating our homes.

Cut that by a fifth and the UK’s total drops by about 3.6%.

Source: National Audit Office, Decarbonising home heating (2024), 2021 data. 3.6% = 20% of 18%.

In the UK, heating our homes is 18% of all emissions. Click: cut it by a fifth and that’s 3.6% of the whole country’s emissions.

So we built one

Heatwise

Heat the rooms people use, not the whole house.

So we built one. We’re [team], and this is Heatwise: heating that warms the rooms you’re in and lets the rest cool.

Heat follows people

Blue: cool or eco · Orange to red: heated

Same house, same three people, same day. On the left, the old way: a timer heats all six rooms, even at midday when everyone is out. On the right, Heatwise: the bathroom is warm for 06:45, the kitchen for breakfast, everything drops to a 12° safety level when the house is empty, and the living room is ready for the evening. The spare room is never used, so it stays cool.

This is the app. Home shows every room now. Plan shows what each room will do today and why. Budget is where you set your weekly money and rules. Impact shows what you saved against a normal timer. Simulation is a live pretend house so you can watch it work. And Ask Luke is a chat with the assistant.

Meet Luke

Give him a budget. He handles the heating.

You decide

  • How much to spend a week
  • How warm rooms should be
  • A repairs allowance

Luke does

  • Heats rooms before you arrive
  • Uses cheap, clean hours
  • Stays within your budget
  • Spots a broken radiator and books a fix

He always asks before he spends money or changes a room.

Luke is the helper inside the app. You set the money and the rules once. He does the rest: warms rooms just before you get there, heats when power is cheap and clean, keeps to the budget, and if a radiator stops working he notices and offers to book an engineer from your repairs allowance. He never acts without asking first.

In our simulation

Warmer, cheaper and cleaner than a timer

15% less

spent and 13% less CO₂ than a normal heating timer

97%

of the time comfortable, compared with 70% for the timer

In a simulated five-room house over a week, Heatwise spent 15% less than a normal timer, with 13% less CO₂, and kept people comfortable 97% of the time instead of 70%. The timer only looks cheap because it leaves people cold. So we also tested against heating left on all the time, which keeps people just as warm: Heatwise is still 16% cheaper with 21% less CO₂. The saving grows with spare rooms, because those are the rooms a timer heats for nobody.
